div.span: The CloudFront-scope web ACL runs first: IP reputation, rate limits, Bot Control labels, body size, protocol version, tool allowlist and argument inspection. Tool names arrive as hello___hello, which the allowlist accepts.

div.span: One front door with a custom domain and edge WAF for a managed endpoint that has neither. /mcp is not cached.

div.span: Pre-filters the token and answers the protected-resource metadata itself: the Gateway’s own document names the Gateway hostname rather than the distribution.

div.b: Public Gateway endpoint, locked by a secret

div.span: The Gateway endpoint is public, so CloudFront sends the secret x-origin-verify header on every origin request.

div.b: Regional AWS WAF on the Gateway

div.span: Default block; only requests with the secret header and an mcp/ scope in x-jwt-claims pass. The lock is the shared secret, checked before the Gateway calls a target.

div.span: The Gateway’s custom JWT authorizer verifies the Cognito token and the mcp/agentcore scope, then invokes the Runtime with SigV4. The Runtime’s inbound authorizer is IAM and admits only the Gateway’s role.
